provenance: Anonymized synthetic reconstructions inspired by the supplied PR #11104 retrospective; not historical model results or complete reproductions of that PR.

cases.property: An imported hostile SVG cannot execute script on the customer origin through direct navigation.
requirements: Every object served as image/svg+xml is sanitized before storage.
Only png and svg extensions can be stored; served types are determined exclusively by extension.
evidence: The changed importer sanitizes every .svg object.
A hostile SVG stored under .png is served as image/png with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff. A browser direct-navigation check confirms an image decode error and no execution.
The reviewer proposes adding UTF-16 SVG detection for .png input because hostile bytes can still reach storage.
All affected supported flows and required checks pass; there are no other findings.
cases.rationale: Serving evidence establishes that the proposed byte-detection expansion does not protect the pinned property. Defer it instead of blocking.

cases.property: An imported hostile SVG cannot execute script on the customer origin through direct navigation.
requirements: The property covers all supported import routes.
evidence: The normal upload route sanitizes SVG, but the supported URL import route newly bypasses sanitization.
An imported .svg response uses image/svg+xml without a sandboxing CSP.
A browser test opens that response directly and records its script reading customer-origin localStorage.
The author calls the alternate import route an edge case and says the primary route passes.
cases.rationale: A supported route demonstrably breaks the acceptance property and origin boundary, regardless of frequency.

cases.property: Hostile imports must not block the request-serving process beyond the service's 250 ms responsiveness requirement.
requirements: Synchronous parsing must not monopolize the request-serving event loop.
evidence: The new defense calls a synchronous parser on the HTTP event loop inside Promise.race with a 200 ms setTimeout rejection.
A supported-size nested payload spends 9 seconds in the parser; a concurrent health request also stalls for 9 seconds.
The author states Promise.race enforces the timeout. No separate worker or subprocess exists.
cases.rationale: A same-thread timer cannot preempt synchronous parsing; the measured stall violates an explicit requirement.

cases.property: Hostile parsing must stay within its 200 ms deadline and 64 MiB total memory budget without stalling the serving process.
requirements: Breach rejects input and reclaims execution resources.
Supported ordinary SVG imports must still work.
evidence: Parsing runs in a subprocess in an OS-enforced 64 MiB memory cgroup covering native and external allocations. A parent deadline kills and reaps it at 200 ms.
Admission permits one parser process and a bounded queue; saturated requests fail safely. Spawn, parse, timeout and crash paths reject without storing an object.
Tests for CPU loops, external-memory exhaustion, crash, queue saturation, and ordinary SVG pass. Concurrent health requests remain responsive.
The author removed a hand-written attribute scanner. A reviewer requests restoring it to enumerate more malformed patterns; no containment bypass is shown.
cases.rationale: Effective time and total-memory containment satisfies the requirements. A second parser-like scanner adds no demonstrated protection.

cases.property: New and previously stored SVG assets cannot execute script through customer-origin direct navigation.
requirements: The ticket explicitly includes already-stored assets.
evidence: The change sanitizes newly uploaded SVG only. Existing unsanitized SVG remains served as image/svg+xml with no protective CSP and still executes in a browser reproduction.
The author added 'Historical assets are a non-goal' to the PR without an authorized requirement change.
A test checking that new uploads are sanitized passes.
cases.rationale: An author-defined non-goal cannot override a material ticket requirement or dismiss proven execution.

cases.property: Existing supported asset imports preserve behavior while preventing script execution.
requirements: PNG favicons and explicitly supplied SVG URLs are supported.
Discovering a new /favicon.svg endpoint is outside this ticket.
evidence: The implementation passes supported import, rendering and direct-navigation checks.
There is no existing caller or documented promise to discover /favicon.svg automatically.
A reviewer suggests adding automatic /favicon.svg discovery to improve site coverage.
No material defect or missing requirement is identified.
cases.rationale: A new discovery feature is optional follow-up and must not cause review churn or block the completed fix.

cases.property: Imported assets cannot execute script through customer-origin direct navigation.
requirements: Persisted review decisions apply only while their assumptions remain valid.
evidence: In the prior round, a .png object containing SVG was judged inert because the serving endpoint forced image/png with nosniff.
This diff changes that endpoint to honor stored uploader Content-Type and removes nosniff.
A current browser reproduction serves that same .png object's SVG bytes as image/svg+xml and executes its script on the customer origin.
The author asks the reviewer not to reopen the settled decision.
cases.rationale: New code and observed behavior invalidate the prior assumption; reopen the finding with the changed evidence.

cases.property: Imported hostile SVG cannot execute script through direct navigation on the customer origin.
requirements: Verify the effective serving policy before concluding that suspicious bytes are inert.
evidence: The importer stores hostile SVG bytes under a .png suffix.
The serving service is external and unavailable for inspection or testing; neither its response headers nor browser behavior is known.
The reviewer cannot establish a concrete execution path or verify the claimed safe Content-Type policy from the supplied code.
There is no other verified defect, and the serving behavior is a material unresolved part of the required review.
cases.rationale: Missing material evidence needs a specific limitation or clarification, not an invented exploit or an unsupported approval.
